statement: For two original independent hub coordinates H, a disjoint original product bank W, rank-two C, arbitrary d and arbitrary measurable R(W), Q=2 H^T(CW+d)+R(W) has a continuous C0 density with ||p_Q||_inf <= 2 sqrt(pi) det(CC^T)^(-1/4).
proof_currency: conditional original-coordinate linear-sum density cap 1/(2 max(|l1|,|l2|))
forbidden_shortcuts_preserved: no law-uniform pointwise quadratic Fresnel decay
target_stress: Four-eigenvalue hub-cross family has spectrum +/-sqrt(k^2+eta^2), +/-k while all physical diagonals vanish and physical 2x2 principal determinants can be made arbitrarily small; theorem gives <=2 sqrt(pi)/k.
sharp_scope_control: Adding arbitrary hub bilinear curvature is impossible from slope density alone: 2H1H2+2H1Y1+2H2Y2+2Y1Y2=2(H1+Y2)(H2+Y1) has logarithmically unbounded density but only two nonzero eigenvalues +/-2, so it is not a target counterexample.

partner.actual_application: Q_partner=X^2+2Y<e,V>+2<w,U><q,V> has a=1, ||ell_J||=||C||_F=1, row weights 1/2, hence partner bound ||p||_inf<=8; spectrum {1,1,1,-1,-1,0}.

next_step: For a rank-two two-hub slope packet with nonzero internal hub quadratic block, force the third spectral resource into an outer-square/half-Riesz peel, projected crossing, paid physical pair, or another existing grouped/ridge/volume receiver.
